sections.label: Updating the Act's aspects
sections.summary: The Bill updates the Act by facilitating MRAs, granting registered surveyors greater professional recognition, and updating penalties and fines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In addition, as the last major amendments to the Act were made 20 years ago, we are also taking the opportunity to update certain aspects of the Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: They are: facilitating the implementation of Mutual Recognition Arrangements (MRAs) between Singapore and other countries or territories and/or between LSB and its foreign counterparts in other countries or territories; granting registered surveyors greater professional recognition; and updating the penalties and fines and dealing with the consequential amendments in the Act.

sections.label: Definition of MRAs
sections.summary: MRAs are bilateral or multilateral arrangements for mutual recognition of registered land surveyors and their survey work between party countries or territories.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As defined in the Bill, MRAs are bilateral or multilateral arrangements for the mutual recognition of land surveyors who are registered in their respective countries or territories and the survey work that may be performed by these land surveyors in each such country or territory that is party to the MRA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will facilitate the movement of local registered surveyors from Singapore who wish to pursue new opportunities overseas, subject to the rules in the foreign jurisdiction.

sections.label: MRA registration provisions
sections.summary: New section 10A lets local registered surveyors apply to LSB for MRA recognition, while clauses 3 to 6 and 9 require LSB and its Registrar to maintain a register of foreign surveyors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: For local registered surveyors intending to engage in survey work overseas under an MRA, the new section 10A, inserted by clause 7 of the Bill, will provide for them to apply to LSB to be recognised for the purposes of that MRA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, for foreign surveyors who wish to carry out survey work in Singapore, clauses 3 to 6 and 9 of the Bill will amend the Act to require LSB and its Registrar to administer and maintain a register of foreign surveyors who have successfully registered with LSB and allow registered foreign surveyors to carry out survey work in Singapore in a manner permitted by LSB pursuant to an MRA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: These changes are supported by the members of LSB, which includes private sector representatives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: They are also in line with the 2017 amendments to the Architects Act 1991 and Professional Engineers Act 1991, which facilitated the implementation of MRAs in these related professional fields.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The amendments proposed in this Bill on MRAs will have the effect of ensuring that local registered surveyors are on par with their allied counterparts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: MRAs can make it easier for local registered surveyors to practise abroad in a participating jurisdiction.

sections.label: ASEAN MRA example
sections.summary: The ASEAN Framework Arrangement for the Mutual Recognition of Surveying Qualifications (ASEAN MRA) was signed in 2007.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: One example is the ASEAN Framework Arrangement for the Mutual Recognition of Surveying Qualifications (ASEAN MRA) which was signed in 2007.

sections.label: ASEAN registered surveyors collaboration
sections.summary: Local registered surveyors recognised as ASEAN registered surveyors can collaborate on land surveying projects in other ASEAN member states.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Local registered surveyors in Singapore who have been recognised as ASEAN registered surveyors will be able to collaborate on land surveying projects in other ASEAN member states.

sections.label: One project condition
sections.summary: LSB intends to impose a condition that foreign registered surveyors under the Scheme take on only one project and collaborate with one local registered surveyor at a time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: When the Scheme is implemented, LSB also intends to impose a condition that foreign registered surveyors under the Scheme will only be able to take on one project and, thus, collaborate with only one local registered surveyor at any one point in time.

sections.label: Unchanged fines since 1991
sections.summary: The quanta of fines and penalties have remained unchanged since the Act was enacted in 1991.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The quanta of fines and penalties have remained unchanged since the Act was enacted in 1991.

sections.label: Clauses raising maximum fines
sections.summary: Clauses 6, 15, 11, 12 and 13 propose raising maximum fines and penalties under several sections of the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Clause 6 proposes to raise the maximum fine in section 10(5), which sets out the penalties for engaging in survey work in Singapore without meeting the requirements stipulated under the Act and falsely representing oneself as a person authorised to supply survey services in Singapore, from $4,000 to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Similarly, clause 15 proposes to raise the maximum fine stated in section 34, which prescribes penalties for the wilful falsification of any register kept under the Act and wrongfully procuring registration under the Act from $4,000 to $10,000, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As for disciplinary proceedings and revocation of licences, clauses 11 and 12 provide for the raising of the maximum penalties under sections 25(2) and 27(2) to $20,000 and $50,000 respectively, from the existing maximum penalties of $10,000 and $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Next, clause 13 will raise the maximum fine under section 30(2) from $2,000 to $5,000.

sections.label: Mutual recognition under MRAs
sections.summary: This is primarily to allow mutual recognition of survey works under MRAs, with the ASEAN MRA on surveying services signed in 2007.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is primarily to allow for mutual recognition of survey works under MRAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I note that the ASEAN MRA on surveying services was signed in 2007.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, even after 17 years later, the detailed scheme has not been fully established.

sections.label: Timeline for ARS scheme
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Minister can provide a timeline for when the details of the ARS scheme will be announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide a timeline for when the details of the ARS scheme will be announced?

sections.label: Cautious approach to Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill's intent but calls for a measured approach, examination of implications on local surveyors, and stringent verification and quality assurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While I commend the intent behind the Land Surveyors (Amendment) Bill to foster greater collaboration and professional recognition within ASEAN, I believe it is imperative that we proceed with a measured and cautious approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must thoroughly examine the potential implications on our local surveyors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We must also ensure that robust measures are in place to sustain the high standards of surveying work that are synonymous with Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, stringent verification of qualifications and rigorous quality assurance mechanisms are non-negotiable aspects of upholding our professional standards.

sections.label: Scheme implementation after details
sections.summary: Passing the Bill does not mean the Scheme is implemented straightaway; it would be implemented after details are ascertained and member states agree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I want to also highlight one very important point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It does not mean that when we passed the Bill, the Scheme is implemented straightaway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It would only be implemented after the details of the Scheme has been ascertained and member states agree to the Scheme as well.

sections.label: Foreign surveyors local collaboration
sections.summary: Registered foreign surveyors may practise in Singapore only in collaboration with local registered surveyors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The other point to note is that registered foreign surveyors would only be allowed to practise in Singapore in collaboration with local registered surveyors.
